rules.text: A ledger entry posted more than 5 business days after the close of its own month, such as a late vendor accrual true-up, goes to the controller for approval.
rules.open_question: When I replayed this rule over the history it matched no entries, so the trail has no example of a late-posted entry. Does the controller have to approve entries posted more than 5 business days after month close, or should this rule be dropped?

rules.text: A Paystream gross charges entry in 1250 Paystream clearing that is 4 days old or less at month end is carried forward to clear against the next month's Paystream payout.
An AP vendor payment entry in 2000 Accounts payable that is 1 day old or less at month end is carried forward to clear against the next month's bank debit.
rules.open_question: The trail agrees with this 2 times and disagrees 0 times. Is this how you want it handled?

rules.text: A Paystream payout whose net agrees with the Paystream payout report is matched to the gross charges in 1250 Paystream clearing, with the report's fees booked to 6310 Payment processing fees, refunds to 4090 Refunds and credits, chargebacks to 6320 Chargeback losses, and any leftover difference to 1290 Unapplied and disputed receipts.
rules.open_question: Most Paystream payouts book refunds to 4090, for example B-BL-00003 and B-BL-00005. But in 5 of about 54 payouts (B-BL-00002, 00023, 00029, 00031 and one more), the staff accountant booked the refund amount to 4000 Subscription revenue. Is 4090 the correct account for Paystream refunds, with the 4000 postings being clerk errors to reclass?

rules.text: A Paystream payout whose net does not agree with the Paystream payout report goes to the controller, who approves parking the unexplained difference in 1290 Unapplied and disputed receipts.
rules.open_question: I see 2 Paystream payouts with part of the difference parked in 1290, both approved by dwhitfield 5 to 9 days later, and I assume the 1290 portion is where the bank net disagreed with the payout report. Is controller approval required whenever the payout does not agree to the report?

rules.text: A customer receipt marked PREPAY with no open invoice is booked in full to 2450 Customer deposits and prepaid commits.
rules.open_question: The trail agrees with this 2 times and disagrees 0 times. Is this how you want it handled?

rules.text: A Halcyon Robotics receipt that is exactly 2% short of its open invoice in 1200 is matched with the 2% booked to 4050 Sales discounts.

A customer receipt that pays several open invoices from the same customer in 1200 Accounts receivable but falls short of their combined total by no more than 12.39 is matched to those invoices, and the unpaid shortfall stays open in 1200 Accounts receivable.
rules.open_question: I see one case (Northwind Logistics, 3 invoices, short by 12.39). A staff accountant posted it 7 days later with the memo 'per Priya'. Can staff leave a small short-pay open in 1200 without asking, or does each one need the AR lead's approval first?

rules.text: A customer receipt short of its open invoices in 1200 by 15.00 to 35.00 is matched with the shortfall booked to 7710 Bank charges as a deducted wire fee.
rules.open_question: I see 2 receipts short by 15.00 and 35.00 booked by staff to 7710, while short-pays of 2.79 and 12.39 went to Priya on the AR team. Is the 7710 treatment only for amounts matching a wire fee, and what is the largest shortfall staff may write off to 7710?

rules.text: A customer receipt short of its open invoices in 1200 by less than 15.00 goes to the AR lead to decide how the short-pay is cleared.
rules.open_question: The trail agrees with this 1 times and disagrees 0 times. Is this how you want it handled?

rules.text: A customer receipt that is short of its open invoices in 1200 Accounts receivable by 0.01 or more goes to the AR lead.
rules.open_question: I found one short-paid receipt: B-BL-00156, a Northwind Logistics wire that paid three invoices and was 12.39 short. It was applied 7 days later with the memo 'per Priya', and the 12.39 was left open in 1200. Do short payments always go to the AR lead, or can the staff accountant leave shortfalls below a certain amount open in 1200 without review? If so, what is that amount?

rules.text: A customer receipt that has no matching open invoice in 1200 Accounts receivable goes to the AR lead to decide how to apply it.
rules.open_question: I see one case (Orbis Freight wire of 218,963.16). It was left open, with AR lead approval still pending and the comment 'see notes'. Should an unmatched customer receipt stay with the AR lead, or should it be parked in 1290 Unapplied and disputed receipts until someone applies it?

rules.text: Sweep account interest credited by the bank is booked in full to 7100 Interest income.
rules.open_question: The trail agrees with this 2 times and disagrees 0 times. Is this how you want it handled?

rules.text: An incoming wire fee or account analysis charge from Commonwealth Trust Bank of 234.15 or less is booked to 7710 Bank charges.
An unexplained bank debit such as a MISC DEBIT goes to the controller before anything is booked to 7710 Bank charges.
rules.open_question: The trail agrees with this 1 times and disagrees 0 times. Is this how you want it handled?

rules.text: A vendor payment leaving the bank by ACH, wire, check or bill pay with no AP payment entry in 2000 Accounts payable goes to the controller to review.
rules.open_question: The trail shows no vendor payment that left the bank without an AP entry in 2000 Accounts payable, so I cannot tell who handles one. Should an unrecorded vendor payment go to the controller or to the AP clerk?
